1.explanation:
To understand how to build a new percent‐based Progress Bar, it’s helpful to examine: 

• ProgressIndicator/ProgressIndicator.mdx — shows Carbon’s existing linear step indicator pattern and ARIA semantics.  
• InlineLoading/InlineLoading.mdx and Loading/Loading.mdx — illustrate how Carbon handles in‐flight states, associated text, and accessible announcements.  
• Slider/Slider.mdx — demonstrates a continuous fill track with a handle, which can inform styling for a non‐interactive progress track.  
• SkeletonPlaceholder/SkeletonPlaceholder.mdx and SkeletonText/SkeletonText.mdx — show placeholder bars and text that mimic progress bars during load, useful as a reference for bar dimensions and animation cues.  

Pulling patterns from these docs will guide the visual style, accessibility, and API design for a new Progress Bar component.
1.bug_scenario: In the provided mockup the installer header shows a continuous, percent‐based progress bar rather than Carbon’s step‐based Progress Indicator. A filled track (green fill on a light gray background) extends to the current percent‐complete, and “1%” is displayed at the right. Above the bar is supporting text (“2 min remaining, 206 Mb/s”), and below is a status line (“Checking CPU on host 9.76.63.174”). This is meant to illustrate a long‐running installation process and give both a visual and numeric sense of completion, plus additional run‐time details.
